subject: english
stem: Which word names a building where soldiers live?
rationale: Barracks are where soldiers live. A hangar houses aircraft, an arsenal stores weapons and a dockyard repairs ships: each a military building, so the item tests knowing the word, not guessing from the setting.

subject: english
stem: Which part of this sentence has an error? "The captain asked us that why we were late for parade."
rationale: A reported question already begins with "why", so "that" is not needed: "The captain asked us why we were late." "That" is carried over from reported statements ("he said that…"), which is the slip this catches.

subject: english
stem: Arrange in order. P. A week later, green shoots appeared. Q. Meena dug a pit in the garden. R. She sowed the seeds and covered them. S. She watered the spot every morning.
rationale: The pit comes first (Q), then the seeds go in it (R), then daily watering (S), and only after a week do shoots appear (P): QRSP. D puts the shoots before the watering that made them grow.

subject: english
stem: When the inspection team arrived, the stores officer was waiting at the gate with his registers. Every shelf had a fresh label, and the floor was still wet from mopping. What can most reasonably be inferred?

options.A: The stores are always kept this clean
options.C: The officer had joined that day
options.D: The officer knew the team was coming

rationale: Fresh labels, a floor still wet and the officer waiting at the gate all point to preparation just before the visit, so he knew it was coming. A goes beyond the passage: recent cleaning says nothing about every day. Nothing is said about faults or his joining.

subject: english
stem: Which part of this sentence has an error? "Hardly had the bus left the stop than it began to rain."
rationale: "Hardly" is followed by "when", not "than": "Hardly had the bus left the stop when it began to rain." "Than" is borrowed from "no sooner … than", the pair it is usually confused with. The inverted "had the bus" in A is correct after "hardly".

subject: english
stem: Though the plan looked ___ on paper, it proved ___ in the field.
rationale: "Though" sets up a contrast, so the two blanks must pull in opposite directions: good on paper, bad in practice. Only "sound … unworkable" does; A, B and C put two words of the same kind together.
